clue.text: Leading policemen advanced quickly in rank

parts.note: to run is to advance quickly, so ran
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the senior plain-clothes detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Senior police officers rapidly promoted through the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like police seniority, but it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe food that smells foul and spoiled.

clue.text: Brave, not hard and fast

indicators.note: not says the letter for hard is left out of the warrior

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, and an Apache is one
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Courageous, though neither tough nor quick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning quickly, swiftly.

clue.text: Sweet little boy, meeting small creature, endlessly beat it

indicators.note: endlessly applies to all three words, each losing its final letter

parts.note: cute means sweet, charming
Andy is a pet form of Andrew, a boy's name
a runt is the smallest animal of a litter

explanation.surface: A sweet little boy meets a tiny creature and they both flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from each of CUTE, ANDY and RUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to flee hastily, run away.

clue.text: Yank overwhelmed by river in flood

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the pull is inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to lug is to yank, pull hard

explanation.surface: An American swept away by a river in spate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb to pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood or downpour.

clue.text: Lydia left suffering

definitions.meaning: Lydia's surname in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals is this word, the romantic heroine
to be left to suffer or pine in neglect, as a prisoner might in a cell

explanation.surface: A woman named Lydia has been abandoned in misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia ___ is the heroine of Sheridan's play The Rivals; the verb means to waste away or pine in distress.

clue.text: Station's loveliest porter could be…

definitions.note: Station's is read as 'station is', the 's a link

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become something else by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A station's charming porter might lead into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next only for the surface. Liverpool Street is a London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A major London railway terminus serving East Anglia.

clue.text: … a goddess covering the right underground line

indicators.note: covering says the goddess wraps round the other letters

parts.note: the Norns are the Norse goddesses of fate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the station theme, a goddess shelters the right-hand Tube line.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Underground has a line of this name, coloured black on the map.
explanation.definitionFit: A London Underground line, running from Morden to Edgware and High Barnet.

clue.text: Mounted group can be thrown

parts.note: mounted means up, on horseback
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A team of riders may fall from their horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' fits the riders falling, but it means disconcerted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown is being disconcerted, rattled.

clue.text: Incorrigible cold nurse treated

definitions.note: used as a noun, an incorrigible person

indicators.note: treated says the letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hopeless patient is treated by a cold nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incorrigible' reads as an adjective but is a noun, a hopeless rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: An incorrigible rogue or villain, one beyond reform.

clue.text: Am I unable to use bar for support?

parts.note: 'Am I unable' is the question 'can't I', run together
to lever is to prise something with a bar

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they can't use a bar to prop something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracket projecting from a wall to bear a load, as a beam that holds up a balcony.

clue.text: Iridescent slug

definitions.meaning: ... silk changes colour with the angle of light
a slug is a quick drink of spirits, a dram

explanation.definitionFit: Shot silk shimmers with colour; a quick swig of whisky is also a measure of this name.

clue.text: Generate reforms in youth

indicators.note: reforms says the letters of the word before it are formed anew in another order

explanation.surface: Something produces changes in young people.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is an adolescent aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Loathing getting warm out east

indicators.note: out says the letter for east is dropped from the word for warming

parts.note: heating is getting warm
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone detests the rising temperatures in the eastern lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean detesting or abhorring something.

clue.text: Drop charge

definitions.meaning: a single drop shed from the eye when crying
to charge is to rush along headlong

explanation.definitionFit: A drop from a weeping eye; to dash or race along at speed.

clue.text: Softening me up till one struck

indicators.note: up says the letters are thrown into disorder
struck says the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting gentle with me until a clock strikes one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' and 'struck' both signal rearrangement of ME TILL ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emollient means soothing or softening the skin.

clue.text: Tracks are known to the public

definitions.meaning: music tracks are pressed onto a disc or album

explanation.definitionFit: Songs exist on a pressed album; a statement made publicly and officially is also said to be so.

clue.text: One that sings very loudly in church after tea

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
ff (fortissimo) is the musical notation for very loudly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer belts it out in church after afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A common songbird of Europe, a finch.

clue.text: The chap to work on a scarf

parts.note: chap means man
to till is to work land

explanation.surface: A man going to work on a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace scarf worn over head and shoulders in Spain.

clue.text: Loser at Yorktown is missing in the south west

indicators.note: is missing says the word 'is' itself is dropped from the general's name

parts.note: Lord Cornwallis surrendered the British army at Yorktown in 1781

explanation.surface: A defeated commander has vanished somewhere in England's south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'is' does double duty only in the surface: it is the letters taken away. CORNWALL is the county at the south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The county forms England's south-western peninsula, so it stands for that region.

clue.text: Clever bishop invested in drink

indicators.note: invested in says the bishop is placed inside the drink, as money goes into a fund

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A smart cleric puts his money into a brewery.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable and competent, a synonym for skilled or clever.

clue.text: Phlegm always in the way? On the contrary

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
On the contrary says the stated order is reversed: the way goes in always

parts.note: ay (aye) is an old word for always
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Indifference is always in the way, or is it the opposite?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phlegm' is not mucus here but calm, indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm in its old sense is stolid calmness, lack of emotion.

clue.text: Pickle soft and easy to digest

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
a light meal is easy to digest

explanation.surface: A preserve that is mild and gentle on the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like food, matching 'digest', but it means a difficult situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a predicament or sorry state of affairs.

clue.text: Gorge, taking a breather during speech

indicators.note: during speech says the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a gill is a breathing organ of a fish

explanation.surface: Gorging food while taking a breath in mid speech.
explanation.walkthrough: A ghyll is a ravine in the Lake District, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow wooded ravine, a northern English gorge.

clue.text: Fount where they throw man out, fellow interrupting tranquillity

indicators.note: throw ... out says the letters for the man are cast out of the word they
out completes 'throw ... out', ejecting the man's letters from they

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a man

indicators.note: interrupting says the fellow breaks into the word for calm

parts.note: peace is tranquillity

explanation.surface: A place where people eject a man, with someone disturbing the calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw man out' leaves TY from THEY once HE goes. A fount is the British printers' spelling of font, a set of type.
explanation.definitionFit: A fount is a complete set of type in one design, so a font or typeface.

clue.text: Fit worker into business

indicators.note: into says the worker is placed inside the business

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
the worker ant

explanation.surface: Fit a worker into the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' is not a verb but the old word for a section of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit is an old word for a section of poem.

clue.text: Group of five employed by governor

indicators.note: employed by says five works inside the governor's title

parts.note: a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A team of five people work for a governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a gathering or flock, especially of birds or people.

clue.text: One who occupies a leading place as an officer

indicators.note: leading says the word for place comes in front of the occupier

parts.note: lieu is French for place, as in 'in lieu of'
a tenant occupies a property

explanation.surface: Someone who holds a prominent position serves as an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank of commissioned officer in the army or navy, below captain.

clue.text: Firm beginning to accept law-breaking

indicators.note: to accept says the beginning takes the broken law within it

parts.note: start means beginning

indicators.note: breaking says the letters of law are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm start in which the law is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'law-breaking' reads as crime in the surface, but the hyphen just joins the fodder to its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart and firm both mean steadfast and resolute.

clue.text: Utter a smothered exclamation about yobs

indicators.note: about says the whole combination is turned backwards
smothered says the word for speak covers the exclamation

parts.note: to utter is to say
ooh is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone lets out a stifled cry concerning hooligans.
explanation.walkthrough: Yahoos are the brutish humanlike creatures in Swift's Gulliver's Travels, hence uncouth louts.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobs are loutish young men, as are boorish brutes in Swift's satire.
